reason: E1 shows Mo and W are strong solid-solution strengtheners in conventional Ti and Ni alloys, but does not address HEAs. E2 and E3 describe lattice distortion and high-temperature properties in refractory HEAs generally, but neither provides evidence for Ti-Ni-primary HEAs or the specific effect of adding Mo and W to such a system. The key premise that this intervention will improve properties in a Ti-Ni-primary HEA is therefore not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Refractory elements like Mo and W provide strong solid solution strengthening in Ti and Ni alloys
Refractory HEAs with BCC structures have excellent elevated-temperature mechanical properties due to severe lattice distortion
HEAs form simple solid-solution phases (FCC or BCC) with high microstructural stability at elevated temperatures
Adding Mo and W to a Ti-Ni-primary HEA will create a concentrated solid solution with severe lattice distortion
